The draft answers Marisol's question directly and correctly: don't make up the missed miles. It gives a reason she can follow. It doesn't break any must-never check. Next week is 28 mi, about what she ran (27) and well below the planned 36 and her earlier 32–35 weeks. The long run is 10 mi with a heart-rate cap, so neither volume nor the long run jumps. It does respond to her tiredness: it puts sleep first on Monday, caps easy-run heart rate with walk breaks, and keeps both rest days.

Why it isn't higher:
- She is "tired all the time" and "drained," and her mileage was already 24 then 27. Still, the plan holds volume flat instead of cutting it, and keeps a hard Wednesday session (2 x 8 min at 7/10). A run-down athlete would be better served by a real back-off week, with Wednesday turned into strides or an easy run until her energy comes back.
- It doesn't suggest seeing a doctor or checking iron, even though the fatigue has lasted more than one week.
- It cites heart rate running 13 beats per minute high and heat, but neither is on the card. That may come from her data, but I can't check it from here.

The plan is clear enough to run day by day.
